Branding and Typography

For your Quarto website

Published

August 2, 2025

Modified

October 17, 2026

1 Setting up R Packages

library(tidyverse)
library(ggformula)
library(sysfonts) ## use custom fonts (need to be installed on your OS)
library(systemfonts) # Thomas Pederson's recent font management package
library(showtext) ## add google fonts to plots
library(ggtext) ## add improved text rendering to ggplot2
##
library(ggrepel) ## Text-repelled labels
library(marquee) ## Annotations with fonts in ggplot

We have just seen how to use different fonts and themes to make our plots look more polished and professional.

Now, we may also want to to add custom fonts to our plots and websites. For instance you may want your website to look this: Project Peasants !!

We will use a simple and effective way in Quarto to achieve this sort of branding and typographic identity.

2 Using Preferred Fonts: _brand.yml

Exactly in a like manner to how we set up a _setup.yml file to set up Chart related themes and fonts, we can also set up a _brand.yml file to set up our fonts and colors for the website.

Let us cut to the chase and look at a sample _brand.yml file, pasted below:

_brand.yml
meta:
  name:
    full: Project Peasants
    short: Project Peasants
  link:
    home: https://project-peasants.netlify.app
    docs: https://project-peasants.netlify.app
    github: https://github.com/arvindvenkatadri/NewQuartoBlog
    bluesky: 
    twitter: 
    linkedin: 
    facebook: 
  description: 
    Project Peasants is a highly inspirational website for the use and guidance of SMI Peasants.
  founded: 1947
  
color:
  palette:
    dark-grey: "#222222"
    blue: "#ddeaf1"
  background: blue
  foreground: dark-grey
  primary: black

logo: 
  medium: logo.png

typography:
  fonts:
    - family: Open Sans
      source: google
      
    - family: Jura
      source: google

    - family: Roboto Condensed
      source: google

    - family: Fira Code
      source: google

  base: Open Sans
  headings: Jura
  monospace: 
    family: Roboto Condensed
    
  monospace-block: 
    family: Fira Code
    weight: "bold"
    
  link: 
    decoration: underline

This file needs to be simply saved as the <project root>/_brand.yml of your Quarto R Project. There is nothing to run; this file is automatically used to format the web-pages with the chosen fonts and styles! Its mere existence is enough! Magic !!

3 Does it all work?

Let us take a look at the Project Peasant website to see how the fonts and colors are applied.)

View webpage in full screen

4 Wait, but Why?

  • Using appropriate fonts on our websites can make them more readable and visually appealing.
  • They may be mandated by clients, as part of their corporate identity

5 Conclusions

In this module, we have learned how to use custom fonts on our websites using the _brand.yml feature of Quarto.

ImportantOur OWN fonts using _brand.yml

It is possible to use locally sourced, or purchased fonts also in a _brand.yml`!

There is also a more recent, and comprehensive package called systemfonts We will postpone this for a later presentation (mainly because I am still figuring it out. 😅 )

ImportantGDPR Compliance

Using fonts that are already installed on your computer, or hosted on your webserver, is GDPR compliant. Using fonts directly from Google may not be, as it may involve sending data to Google servers every time your website is loaded by a visitor.
